title: Clopen factorization and restriction uniqueness for proper/open sheaf maps
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; their structure maps are not required to be separated [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each $T$, choose either $\mathscr M_T=\operatorname{Mod}((A_n)_T)$ at one fixed $n$, or the category $\mathscr M_T$ of module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_T$ with semilinear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$ and compatible componentwise morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathscr M_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme map $f$ write $f^*$ for exact constant-coefficient module inverse image and $P_f=D(f^*)$; for an open immersion $j$ write $j_!$ for exact extension by zero and $J_j=D(j_!)$. Use the specified adjunctions $P_f\dashv S_f=Rf_*$ and $J_j\dashv P_j$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. System operations are constructed simultaneously on the ringed diagram site, before finite evaluation, scalar restriction or total limit [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Let $k_1:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ be quasi-compact open immersions, let $r:U\to W$ and $p:V\to Z$ be proper, and assume $pk_1=ir$. Put $V_W=V\times_ZW$, with projections $b:V_W\to V$, $q:V_W\to W$, and induced map $s=(k_1,r):U\to V_W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed on this square.

The map $b$ is open, $q$ is separated, $s$ is both open and proper and hence a closed immersion, and $V_W$ is of finite type over $k$. In particular $V_W=s(U)\amalg C$, with $C=V_W\setminus s(U)$ an open subscheme. For either coefficient category, restriction gives an exact equivalence
$$\mathscr M_{V_W}\simeq\mathscr M_U\times\mathscr M_C.$$
Its inverse sends $(F_U,F_C)$ to the module sheaf, or system of module sheaves, whose sections on $T\to V_W$ are $F_U(T\times_{V_W}U)\times F_C(T\times_{V_W}C)$. In the system case this inverse commutes with restriction of scalars and with all semilinear transitions. Under this equivalence, $s_!G=(G,0)$ and the canonical projector $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^*F$ is $(1,0)$.

For arbitrary $F\in\mathscr M_{V_W}$ and $G\in\mathscr M_U$, restriction, followed by the identity open unit, gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathscr M_V}(b_!F,(k_1)_!G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathscr M_U}(s^*F,G).$$
Thus two such sheaf or system maps are equal whenever their restrictions to $U$ agree. For $M\in\mathscr M_W$, the underived open-unit comparison $p^*i_!M\cong b_!q^*M$ identifies its source with $b_!q^*M$, and the bijection applies with $F=q^*M$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The bijection is asserted in the abelian sheaf and system categories; no faithfulness of evaluation on derived morphisms is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the gluing inverse as the explicit binary product of direct images on the actual ringed site: the small pro-etale site for one level, the coefficient-sequence site for systems. Restriction along an open is the explicit pushforward along the open-site map with inverse constant-ring transpose. The existing open-site adjunction identifies it with the specified inverse image by uniqueness of left adjoints. The disjoint-open section decomposition proves the gluing unit invertible. For the counit, the diagonal test map is invertible and the off-diagonal test object is empty, so projection followed by diagonal restriction is bijective. These give an equivalence whose inverse has literal product sections. Equivalences preserve finite limits and colimits. Scalar, test restriction, morphism and transition compatibilities are the componentwise formulas of this construction. The existing evaluation_smul helper computes scalar transport through the coefficient-ring equality; it does not use the open-scalar-preservation theorem. Underlying abelian sections forget the sequence-ring action before fixed-level presheaf evaluation; this is the same carrier and additive data as module evaluation, with no scalar-transport expansion.

proof.text: Apply full faithfulness of b_!, obtained from its invertible adjunction unit. The isomorphism k^* ≅ b^* followed by s^* is the specified pullback compositor and squareLift projection equality. Conjugate this isomorphism through the composite open adjunction to identify b_!s_! with k_!. In the product equivalence, a map to s_!G has zero complementary component and first component a map to s^*s_!G; compose with the inverse open unit. This is a bijection. The conjugate-equivalence unit identity gives exactly the restrictionSource formula. Cancellation of the open unit proves naturality in both variables and injectivity of restriction.

Their moduleSquareG_eq theorem specifies the original three-factor compositor expression, so this is the same canonical comparison. Use the proved ordinary openBetaModule normalization at one level. For systems use moduleBeta, whose inverse is defined as the open adjunct of the pullback of the unit followed by moduleSquareG inverse. The adjunction hom-equivalence identity gives exactly the beta unit equation.

lean.statement: theorem ambientClopenRestrictionUniqueness (K : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (_hl : l ≠ K.p) (U V W Z : Over (Spec (.of K.k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom] [QuasiCompact U.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType V.hom] [QuasiCompact V.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType W.hom] [QuasiCompact W.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom] [QuasiCompact Z.hom] (k : U ⟶ V) (r : U ⟶ W) (p : V ⟶ Z) (i : W ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion k.left] [IsOpenImmersion i.left] [QuasiCompact k.left] [QuasiCompact i.left] [IsProper r.left] [IsProper p.left] (h : k.left ≫ p.left = r.left ≫ i.left) : IsOpenImmersion (pullback.fst p.left i.left) ∧ IsSeparated (pullback.snd p.left i.left) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (StrictTower.squareLift k.left r.left p.left i.left h) ∧ IsProper (StrictTower.squareLift k.left r.left p.left i.left h) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (StrictTower.squareLift k.left r.left p.left i.left h) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (pullback.snd p.left i.left ≫ W.hom) ∧ QuasiCompact (pullback.snd p.left i.left ≫ W.hom) ∧ ∀ m : Option ℕ, Assertion l E m k.left r.left p.left i.left h
